overview: After 1.c4 g5 Black offers the g-pawn and White answers 2.d4 Bg7, the Myers Defence with the bishop hitting d4 and b2. White can take with 3.dxg5 or 3.Bxg5 and play for a space edge, while Black seeks development and pressure on the long diagonal. It is a rare, offbeat line.

white_ideas.idea: Take the g5 pawn and develop quickly with Nc3 and e3
Hold the d4 pawn and keep the extra pawn

black_ideas.idea: Use the long diagonal against b2 and d4
Develop fast and attack the White centre with ...d6 and ...c5

character.notes: Black risks a pawn for activity, so the game is concrete.

gambit.notes: White can take on g5 and keep the pawn.

soundness.notes: The line is considered inferior for Black.

structure.notes: The centre is undefined but pieces get open diagonals.

level.notes: Plans are loose and there is little main theory.

character.reason: Black plays a gambit and the position becomes concrete.

gambit.reason: Black gives up the g-pawn, which White can keep.

soundness.reason: The early g5 push is generally seen as inferior for Black.

level.reason: A dubious line cannot be Beginner.

plans.reason: Black's bishop on g7 is the main idea.
